newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to tighten security at federal dams.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to tighten security at federal dams.

text.p: Responding to increased concerns about terrorism since the 1995 bombing of a government building in Oklahoma City, a federal agency said Thursday it will tighten security at the dams it manages.
"There's a potential danger out there that we need to address," Eluid Martinez, commissioner of the Bureau of Reclamation, said at a briefing.

Martinez said the agency will add an independent security and safety office to review and if necessary upgrade equipment and procedures to prevent terrorist incidents at dams including such giants as the Hoover Dam in Arizona and Nevada and the Grand Coulee in Washington.
He said the agency, which owns some 475 dams and dikes in Western states, will spend about $15 million over the next three years to improve security.
Martinez said this was not in response to any specific threat and declined to say whether there were particular dams viewed as potential problems.

Martinez also released a report by a panel of engineers that said the agency had an effective overall program to ensure the structural safety and security of its aging dams, but cited some shortcomings.

The report recommended adding the safety and security officer who would report directly to the bureau commissioner, and said funds to maintain the dams could be used more efficiently to avoid deferring maintenance work.
